# Jumi

> Jumi writes CSS animations through Tailwind CSS v4. 235 effects, 395 property targets, keyframes written inside a class name, per-property timing, a stagger, scroll-driven timelines and view transitions, all generated at build time with no runtime in the browser.

Jumi is a Tailwind plugin plus an integration, and the two are not interchangeable: the plugin
teaches Tailwind the utilities, and the integration completes the stylesheet once every `animate-*`
class has been compiled. Wiring only the plugin compiles the utilities, animates nothing and warns
about nothing, which is why the guides start there.

## Guides

- [Introduction](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/): Jumi is a motion vocabulary for Tailwind CSS. Start with an effect, then make every part your own.
- [Installation](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/installation/): Install the plugin, wire it into your build, and make your first entrance.
- [The build step](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/build-step/): Jumi is a plugin plus an integration, because the animation lists are assembled after Tailwind compiles. Here is what that means, and what it costs you.
- [Composing motion](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/properties/): Animate property targets directly. Give simple pieces a shared purpose.
- [Reveals & exits](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/reveals/): Angular wipes, parallel apertures, hinge exits and a feathered-mask recipe.
- [Sized effects](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/sizing-effects/): What accordion, typing and the expand family need from the box they animate.
- [Timing & controls](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/controls/): Control how an animation begins, travels, repeats, and settles.
- [Stagger](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/stagger/): One motion, passed from child to child. No JavaScript loop required.
- [Transitions](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/transitions/): Smooth the change on hover, focus, or any other change of style.
- [View transitions](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/view-transitions/): Animate the browser's own view transition, on the outgoing and incoming sides.
- [Same-document](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/same-document-transitions/): One wrapper around your state change, and the browser does the rest.
- [Accessible motion](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/docs/accessibility/): Good motion includes the option to experience less of it.

## Reference

- [The effect catalog](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/effects/): every one of the 235 effects, searchable, with a preview for each.
- [llms-full.txt](https://jumi-css.vercel.app/llms-full.txt): every guide, plus the agent skill, in one file.
- [The agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ibnlanre/jumi/main/SKILL.md): the whole vocabulary as one markdown file, written for a coding agent, including all 235 effect names and all 395 property utilities.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ibnlanre/jumi): version 0.1.0.
- [Source](https://github.com/ibnlanre/jumi).
